controls_and_unresolved_spans.basis: Existing source-audited contributor rule; official catalog and OPF separately credit Jowett as translator. Dialogue books are not matched.
The preface is signed A. EINSTEIN and datedDecember1916. A Preface heading alone is not evidence of another contributor.
The introduction recounts Darwin’s Beagle work in the first person and explains his own research.
Darwin’s own revised first-person introduction is distinct from the digital edition notice.
The introductions explain the author’s plan and the appendix adds material to his argument; no separate commentator identity established.
Hobbes’s signed dedication and authored introduction are distinct from the preceding ASCII transcription note.
Nietzsche’s dated preface and translated closing poem are authored literary content. Magnus’s translator heading does not make the poem editorial prose.
I. Introduction is the opening narrated scene of Wells’s fiction, not an external editor’s introduction.

The Etymology/Extracts framing includes Melville’s literary devices and an anthology of individually credited quotations. It needs nested quotation attribution, not a generic external-editor assumption.
Inline chapter notes carry B. signatures and references. An initial is insufficient to name a personal editor; relabeling whole chapters would misattribute Voltaire’s main text.
Footnotes name and quote Burd and other sources within main chapters. Preserve those local credits; an unsigned note compiler cannot be inferred from the translator credit.
A note for Miss Bennet is part of a chapter heading/caption, and the section is Austen’s narrative. Keyword note is insufficient.
